messages:
iona: Filing this here since CI started failing after the docs migration. Linkcheck + HTML render show extra trailing paren for inline code examples when the code contains a closing paren. paul: Seen that before. Usually happens when linkify runs on inline code inside parentheses. Example from the renderer: ```

Call client with create_user('alice')) to add a user.

``` Note the extra ) after the code block. matcha-bot: CI: docs/linkchecker reported 9 anchor/URL issues in the last run (build 789). iona: Workarounds: 1) wrap inline code in angle brackets like `create_user('alice')` in docs (ugly), 2) escape trailing paren in the source `create_user('alice')\)` or 3) adjust markdown-it/linkify options so it doesn't munge code tokens. ryan: I can patch the markdown pipeline: ensure the fence/code renderer runs before linkify. That fixed it in our other repo. I'll check which plugin order is used in the current docusaurus config. paul: If you change the parser ordering, add a test that exercises `renderInline('call `foo()`);` so we don't regress. Also flagging that a lot of examples live in content/sdk and content/examples. iona: Plan: ryan will try parser ordering tweak in a branch and add a minimal test; paul will open a small PR to escape the three most visible offending examples so main isn't blocked; I'll add a temporary linkcheck exception for the affected files. ryan: Opening branch `docs/avoid-linkify-before-code` and will push a test + patch. ETA EOD. paul: I'll push the escape patch to `docs/quickfix/paren-examples` and reference this thread. iona: Thanks — once ryan's change lands we can revert the quickfixes. Please add a short note to the docs migration guide about the parser ordering difference and the recommended pattern: prefer fenced blocks or explicit HTML anchors for tricky inline examples. :memo:
